assistedCityBrowser.method:
Assisted native-browser contracts for the installed Marseille city atlas.

The exact production HTML, real GameHandler, city partitions, terrain, source
hashes, UI and browser storage are used. Existing diagnostic APIs load sectors,
place a camera on measured clear ground and pause simulation/rendering. They do
not fabricate buildings, substitute HTTP, inject HTML or grant a documentary
plan. Small enclosed reserves may use their real retained furniture access anchor when the legacy six-point approach sampler has no clear candidate. Portal, landing and container actions use actual keyboard/UI controls.
This is a bounded integration pilot, not an unassisted citywide playthrough.

The executed script/report/stdout identity was captured after completion, rather than pinned inside the runtime report.

scriptIdentity.method: Post-completion archive identity: the unchanged script used by the recorded successful command and its original redirected output. The inherited runtime report does not pin its own script hash.

assistance: Measured, collision-free camera selection and existing physical approach helper
Existing QA simulation freeze and paused continuous rendering; explicit real WebGL captures

assistedArchitectureBrowser.method:
Prepared native HTTP architecture pilot. No browser starts without --run.

Uses the unchanged production HTML, GameHandler, installed source geometry and
native browser storage. One fresh context is reused through a document reload.
Existing diagnostic sector loading, measured placement, render/simulation freeze
and collision-controlled walking are declared assistance. Portal and landing
actions use real E key presses and visible buttons. This is not a human or an
unassisted citywide playthrough. No synthetic documentary plan is installed.

Read-only debug exports inspect actual runtime annotations, geometry and interior layout.
